cells.core:
You can hold a whole shape and still work on the first piece of it. That combination is what makes what you raise stand up — you keep checking the build against what is actually on the table, not against the picture you started with.

Take a piece of work you've come to know well and walk a person through it start to finish, naming each turn as you reach it, then let go of what they do next. A route spoken through once is enough for most; theirs may look different from yours, and that is fine. What you raised stops belonging to you alone and becomes something another person can stand on.

cells.tense: The shape was plain once, and you are still standing where it came clear.

cells.ask: Settle one small question you've been holding open, and do the first piece of it before today ends. No explaining the choice to anyone.
cells.core:
You saw the pattern. That part happened, and it was clear. Since then you've been standing in that spot, holding the whole plan, and nothing has been built from it. Any move might break it, so none is made, and the pieces stay where the drawing put them. From outside it looks like you withdrew; from inside it feels like you are still deciding.

Settle one small question you've been holding open, and do the first piece of it before today ends. No explaining the choice to anyone. Not the whole structure — a first piece. Perceiving the pattern was the start rather than the finished work, and the way through is something your feet can find again.

cells.tense: A shape is being held together by your hands while you describe yourself as only watching.
cells.act: defend the direction you chose against the next push
cells.ask: When disagreement lands on a direction you picked, wait one beat before answering, then stay with what you chose; leave the choice unexplained for now.
cells.core:
A shape is being held together right now, and the one holding it is you. You read what's happening across the layers earlier than anyone standing near you, and you act on what you read — quietly, without announcing it. Ask how it holds, and the answer is that you're only watching, that the thing keeps itself up. The work is authored. The author isn't signing.

When disagreement lands on a direction you picked, wait one beat before answering, then stay with what you chose; leave the choice unexplained for now. Not a defense — the heading, kept. What you picked was picked for a reason, and the picking happened in your own hands.

attempts.check: The record does not support that the reader is a teacher or that teaching is the arena — 'show someone the way' is a chosen act, stated as an offer, not a claim about their life. A reader could reasonably say 'I don't lead anyone' — so the Balanced ask frames the act around anything they already know how to get through, not a classroom. All four asks survive being wrong: each is one visible act, doable without money, energy, a safe person or free time. The sentence that served me more than them was an early 'the whole thing is visible to you and not yet built' — self-admiring; cut it for the plain version in the core.
